newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-FRANZ BREAKS WRIST, TO MISS GARMISCH.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FRANZ BREAKS WRIST, TO MISS GARMISCH.

text.p: Austrian Werner Franz broke his right wrist and chipped a bone in his left heel after falling in the downhill at the Alpine skiing world championships on Saturday.
Werner Margreiter, head coach of the Austrian men's team, said Franz had also broken a bone in his hand and would miss the next World Cup downhill in Garmisch in Germany on February 21.
"(He) skied very badly at the top and he then took too many risks," said Margreiter. Franz lost his balance on a curve and crashed feet forwards into safety netting.
Franz is third in the World Cup downhill standings, the highest-ranked Austrian skier. He will travel back to Austria on Sunday and undergo surgery in Innsbruck.

"I will definitely miss Garmisch but I hope to be back at the beginning of March for the downhill in Kvitfjell," said Franz. "There's no point thinking about what happened. I will just have to do better next time."
